component.name: NV Broadcast
component.summary: AI-powered virtual camera with background removal and meeting transcription

description.p: NV Broadcast brings NVIDIA Broadcast features to Linux. AI-powered virtual camera with background removal, eye contact correction, face relighting, voice studio, and meeting transcription — all running locally on your GPU.
Features:

ul.li: Background blur, replace, or remove with 3 AI models
Eye contact correction — look at camera while reading your screen
Face relighting — fill light guided by the scene
Voice studio — bass, treble, warmth, compression with GPU acceleration
AI meeting transcription — local Whisper, no cloud
AI meeting summarizer — action items, questions, key points
Recording with NVENC hardware encoding to MP4
9 processing modes including Killer, Zeus, DocZeus, CUDA, and CPU fallback
5 built-in profiles: Meeting, Streaming, Presentation, Gaming, Clean
Works with Zoom, Chrome, OBS, Discord, FaceTime

description.p: Camera recovery and first public v1.5 release

ul.li: Retried advertised camera encodings at the same resolution and frame rate when the preferred mode failed before producing a frame
Allowed the strict Snap's isolated meeting-transcription worker to use a private shared-memory namespace
Required pip 26.2 or newer in source and native-package installers
Selected a supported Python 3.11-3.13 interpreter and validated matching desktop bindings for source installs
Required every Snap Store action to resolve to a validated release tag and source commit before build or upload
Added cumulative in-app contributor credits and a pull-request credit check
Carried forward the v1.5.1 safe native-upgrade helper, clean uninstall, verified runtimes, device recovery, and release provenance

description.p: Native upgrade and release gate hotfix

ul.li: Added an attested native-package helper bound to exact release hashes for safe upgrades from affected legacy DEB and RPM scripts
Validated package identity, version, architecture, installed version, and known maintainer-script content before privileged upgrade work
Removed installer-generated virtual environments, build metadata, and bytecode on final native-package uninstall
Prevented Snap review or candidate dispatches from publishing draft GitHub releases
Retained deterministic runtime ownership, fresh-process acceleration probes, device recovery, and Linux arm64 face effects from v1.5.0

description.p: Verified runtimes, safer packaging, and startup recovery

ul.li: Enforced exactly one CPU or CUDA ONNX Runtime distribution owner across source, native-package, macOS, and Snap environments
Verified CPU, CUDA, and TensorRT readiness through pinned fresh-process model execution and rejected silent provider fallback
Added explicit source runtime selection with clean CPU recovery for failed automatic CUDA setup and restart-gated runtime changes
Restored saved microphone selection, persisted a visible fallback, and rebuilt the active audio pipeline when the device changes
Stopped GUI and headless startup cleanly when no usable physical camera is available
Made profile auto-start an explicit per-profile opt-in and kept UI state aligned after failed starts
Added MediaPipe 1.0.0 face effects on Linux arm64 and raised dependency security floors
Strengthened strict Snap runtime validation, reviewed revision promotion, rollback, and Store metadata refresh
Published deterministic SHA-256 manifests for native packages and attached Snap assets, plus GitHub provenance for every tag-built package
Required exact-tag and commit provenance verification for both Snap architectures before stable promotion

description.p: Global controls, Gaze Lock, and live video reliability update

ul.li: Added rebindable Linux global shortcuts for background, Auto Frame, Eye Contact, Mirror, and microphone noise-removal toggles
Added Natural and Gaze Lock Eye Contact modes with coordinated binocular targeting and conservative blink fallback
Added live physical-camera switching and fixed profile changes for single-frame video backends
Rebuilt and atomically swapped RVM sessions during quality or processing-mode changes, with clean CUDA recovery and CPU fallback
Preserved more fine head-hair and facial-hair detail in Ultra quality while suppressing neutral or bright background spill on soft replacement edges
Kept microphone capture active so Pulse/PipeWire clients do not retain multi-second latency after opening an idle virtual microphone
Bound Protobuf to the patched 5.29.6 through 6.x range for compatibility with system-site Python packages
Used one bounded OpenCV 4 owner, staged complete Snap runtime dependencies, and validated dependency closure before artifact upload
Prevented Snap, DEB, and RPM installs from modifying package-managed Python runtimes through the GUI and removed pip from Snap runtime artifacts
Removed GTK image baseline warnings and harmonized runtime log prefixes

description.p: GPU video, power save, and background quality update

ul.li: Added a device-resident NVIDIA video path with pinned transfers, CUDA color conversion, GPU matte processing, and optional nvImageCodec MJPEG decode
Made background blur substantially stronger and added separate Dim and Desaturate controls with matched GPU and CPU behavior
Added conservative camera and microphone power saving that keeps virtual devices available and treats uncertain consumer state as active
Fixed physical camera selection and native capture negotiation on supported Apple Silicon Macs
Removed saturated physical-background color from sunlit replacement edges and fixed direct GPU virtual-camera negotiation on Linux
Kept Linux arm64 on patched Protobuf while safely disabling MediaPipe-dependent face effects until a compatible upstream wheel is available
Retained staged automatic fallback when GPU decode, conversion, or frame processing is unavailable

description.p: Backlit matting stability patch

ul.li: Improved Quality and Ultra background mattes when strong highlights and deep foreground shadows appear together
Adapted only the RVM model input while preserving original camera colors in displayed and virtual-camera output
Smoothed backlight adaptation over time and returned automatically to neutral processing in balanced lighting
Added regressions for lighting classification, recovery, performance-mode bypass, and input-frame integrity

description.p: Binocular eye contact and latency patch

ul.li: Derived one shared camera-facing correction from both eyes instead of centering each iris independently
Preserved natural iris spacing with a small outward target and conservative head-yaw compensation
Reduced latency for coordinated gaze while retaining stronger smoothing for unstable one-eye landmarks
Tapered extreme side-gaze correction and skipped both eyes during blinks or asymmetric detections

description.p: Eye contact visibility patch

ul.li: Made moderate gaze correction visible at the persisted default intensity instead of producing a sub-pixel no-op
Corrected horizontal and vertical gaze inside a feathered eyelid contour while preserving frame alpha
Smoothed gaze movement between frames and rejected blinks or unstable landmark offsets
Kept the corrected contiguous BGR output path for OBS Virtual Camera on supported Apple Silicon Macs

description.p: Community audio, performance, and camera update

ul.li: Added DeepFilterNet3 neural noise removal with checksum-verified model downloads and automatic RNNoise fallback
Reduced idle CPU use by capping ONNX Runtime thread pools and enabling blocking CUDA synchronization by default
Added a native StatusNotifierItem tray with explicit shutdown cleanup and a legacy fallback
Made the Linux virtual-camera output device configurable across the app, headless service, and installer
Made config saves atomic, kept persistent logs private, and aligned voice effects across app and helper paths
Stored first-run AI models in a writable per-user cache and verified downloads against pinned SHA-256 digests

description.p: Auto Frame tracking and framing patch

ul.li: Smoothed Center Face lateral tracking so small side-to-side movement no longer waits for a large crop jump
Added an Auto Frame Framing selector with Center Face and Stable Background modes
Kept Center Face framing active at minimum zoom by reserving a small internal tracking crop margin
Made switching from Stable Background back to Center Face take effect on the next detected face
Added regression tests for tracking smoothness, mode switching, config persistence, and minimum-zoom behavior

description.p: OBS startup, phone webcam, and audio filtering patch

ul.li: Stopped the optional headless virtual-camera service before the main app opens the camera, avoiding blank preview and busy-camera conflicts after login
Improved Android and phone-as-webcam fallback behavior with safer mode retries and clearer busy-camera diagnostics
Installed the PyAV dependency with the core app so RNNoise mic and speaker cleanup can initialize reliably
Kept meeting transcription and summaries on the bundled faster-whisper runtime path with the required support packages
Improved virtual-camera setup recovery for existing installs without reloading the camera while other apps are using it

description.p: OBS camera compatibility and packaging reliability patch

ul.li: Fixed white preview and missing-effects cases on cameras that expose raw video modes instead of MJPEG for the selected resolution
Avoided stale, metadata-only, and virtual-loopback camera nodes during startup after device order changes
Updated the headless virtual camera command to use the same camera compatibility path as the main app
Fixed CUDA runtime package paths for source, Debian, RPM, and amd64 Snap installs
Added regression tests for raw-camera fallback, camera-node filtering, headless virtual camera behavior, and package metadata consistency

description.p: Live edge quality, compute control, and sponsor visibility update

ul.li: Improved background replacement stability around hair, shoulders, raised hands, and finger gaps during motion
Applied replace-mode fringe cleanup in the fused CUDA compositing path and reduced the CPU cost of edge cleanup
Added Auto, GPU Focused, and CPU Focused compute controls so users can choose the best performance tradeoff for their system
Kept meeting transcription packaging on the lighter faster-whisper runtime while guarding openai-whisper for compatible Python versions only
Added visible GitHub Sponsors walls and About-window backer recognition

description.p: Meeting runtime dependency hotfix

ul.li: Fixed the local meeting transcription runtime installer so faster-whisper support packages keep their required dependencies
Updated Debian, RPM, and macOS package install paths to use the same corrected meeting runtime recipe
Improved missing-transcription help text so users see the complete recovery command
Kept openai-whisper optional and guarded on newer Python versions while packaged installs use the lighter faster-whisper runtime

description.p: Audio helper and installer reliability patch

ul.li: Stopped stale orphaned audio helpers from feeding duplicate nvbroadcast mic audio after the app exits
Cleaned old audio helpers before starting a new one, reducing echo-like doubled microphone audio in calls
Fixed the source installer CuPy verification flow so optional GPU package checks do not abort the whole install incorrectly
Improved installer error reporting so failed optional GPU checks show the real exit code and useful output
Made project sponsorship links easier to find from the app and README

description.p: Live edge quality and microphone reliability patch

ul.li: Improved background replace around hair edges, finger gaps, and hands near the body during motion
Improved live quality-mode behavior so motion edges stay fresher and trail less during movement
Reduced beautify and relighting spill into head hair so hair looks more natural and less washed out
Tuned the live GPU background path and shared face-effect flow for steadier real-time behavior
Kept the exported nvbroadcast microphone available even when voice effects and noise removal are turned off
Rechecked audio, video, meeting transcription, summaries, and packaging paths before release

description.p: Live background performance and stability patch

ul.li: Fixed the live background alpha path so one dedicated worker owns CUDA inference instead of many short-lived threads
Stopped repeated invalid-resource-handle failures and RVM state-reset loops that could make replace mode extremely laggy
Relighting now reuses the same-frame final matte, and replace-mode live processing caches more work instead of rebuilding it twice
Beautify keeps more GPU work inside the face ROI and preserves raw denoise history more carefully to reduce motion smear around the face and glasses

description.p: Stability and live-quality patch for meetings and streaming

ul.li: Stabilized effect and mode switching so the camera path is less likely to freeze, die, or hit device-busy teardown races
Fixed TensorRT detection for current tensorrt-cu12 package layouts and improved Zeus/Killer runtime handoff
Cleaned duplicate nvbroadcast mic and speaker entries and reduced startup audio restore churn
Scoped beautify denoise to the face ROI to reduce motion smear on the face and glasses
Reduced false replace-mode shoulder and underarm background breakout during raised-hand overlap

description.p: Audio and packaging reliability patch for meetings

ul.li: Stabilized the processed nvbroadcast microphone so browser and meeting apps can open it reliably on Linux
Fixed optional Whisper runtime validation and included the missing httpx dependency in the in-app installer path
Release installers now package the local meeting transcription runtime more consistently
Saved meeting finalization now reads the app's WAV capture directly instead of depending on an external ffmpeg binary
Release smoke and packaging CI now cover the meeting runtime path and are opted into Node 24

description.p: Meeting-first live quality and packaging update

ul.li: Reduced visible live delay by preferring fresh video frames and dropping stale buffers under load
Added persistent Auto - Adaptive tuning with weak-device warnings and capture-mode recommendations
Made face relighting brighten-biased and softened eye-contact behavior for more natural live meetings
Exposed the processed microphone as nvbroadcast and fixed speaker denoise to honor the selected output device
Improved update surfacing for GitHub releases, Snap installs, and macOS package downloads

description.p: Priority stability and meeting-quality update

ul.li: Improved final meeting transcript quality with better chunk cleanup and full-audio finalization
Moved meeting transcript, notes, and summary finalization off the UI thread to avoid end-meeting hangs
Persisted speaker selection and active profile state across restarts
Added reset-to-defaults for returning to a known-good setup quickly
Fixed microphone test recording and playback and expanded test duration choices to 30s, 45s, and 60s

description.p: Stability and live-quality patch

ul.li: Stabilized the Linux virtual-camera sink path on v4l2loopback devices
Reduced live video lag by reusing face landmarks and limiting relighting to the face ROI
Tightened replace-mode edges around shoulders, hair, ears, and under-arm gaps
Improved local meeting transcription startup, chunk size, and saved meeting audio reliability
Resolution changes now save safely without hanging the live stream and apply after restart

description.p: Meeting assistant and guided runtime-install update

ul.li: New collapsible meeting sidebar with live local transcript and summary
Meeting history now stays on-device for 7 days and opens from the app
Meeting capture now records both-way audio for better notes and transcripts
Optional runtimes install in the background from the app with progress tracking
First-run setup now explains modes, skip flow, and required downloads more clearly

description.p: Background quality and release-readiness update

ul.li: Tighter replace and remove mattes with better edge stability
Improved premium mode restore and startup consistency
Packaged CSS and desktop assets now ship correctly in wheels
Standard installer now performs a regular install instead of editable mode
Added release smoke checks for compile, tests, and wheel asset validation

description.p: AI Release — v1.0.0

ul.li: AI meeting transcription (local Whisper, GPU-accelerated)
AI meeting summarizer (action items, key points)
Voice studio with 6 presets and GPU acceleration
Microphone and speaker selection
Audio VU meter and mic test
Recording with audio (NVENC + AAC)

description.p: Eye contact, relighting, Apple-like UI, profiles, macOS support
9 processing modes, edge refinement, video enhancement, system tray
